sections.h2: How can I sell my house fast in Hamilton Township, Mercer County, NJ?
sections.html:
Owners in this Hamilton can list, sell privately or take a cash offer, and the schedule hinges on a Certificate of Approval from the township's housing inspectors, a tax payoff and a recorded deed. This page covers Hamilton Township next to Trenton, not the Atlantic County township of the same name.

It is the most populous municipality in Mercer County, with a Census Bureau estimate of 94,157 residents for July 1, 2025. About 71.6 percent of homes are owner-occupied and the median value is $335,500.

sections.h2: What is Hamilton Township like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Hamilton Township covers 39.44 square miles and is the largest suburb of Trenton, the state capital, which lies to its west. Despite its size it has no true downtown. Several communities form separate commercial centers instead: Mercerville (13,447 residents in 2020), Hamilton Square (12,679), White Horse (9,791), Yardville (6,965) and Groveville (3,106).

The township was incorporated on April 11, 1842, and takes its name from Hamilton Square. Open space is a selling point: Veterans Park covers 350 acres inside the township, Mercer County Park's 2,500 acres adjoin it to the north, and Grounds For Sculpture occupies 42 acres. New retirement communities and assisted-living facilities have gone up near Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital Hamilton, and new restaurants, banks and stores have opened along Route 33.

  • Mercerville and Hamilton Square: the two most populous census-designated places.
  • White Horse: in the southern part of the township, where the 1733 Isaac Pearson House stands.
  • Groveville: the smallest of the five census-designated places, with 3,106 residents in 2020.

One local quirk affects buyers and mail: the Postal Service officially treats many Hamilton addresses as Trenton, so confirm the township when you advertise the house.

sections.html:

The state's 2025 general tax rate for the township is 3.708 per $100, with an effective rate of 2.434. The average sale price sits well above the median value reported to the Census, which shows why recent comparable sales matter more than older averages.

sections.h2: What approval does Hamilton Township require before a house changes hands?
sections.html:
Before any change in occupancy of a house, dwelling or apartment, the township's Office of Housing Inspection and Landlord Compliance must issue a Certificate of Approval. Hamilton Township says the building and premises must meet township ordinances, and that life safety is the first priority of the inspection.

You can apply through the Change of Occupancy Application Portal or submit paper forms to the office. The office also publishes a Change of Occupancy Checklist, and walking through it before the inspector arrives is the cheapest way to avoid a repeat visit. The township does not inspect houses for lead on request, so a seller who wants a lead test must hire an inspector.

  • Apply once you have a signed contract, so the approval is fresh at closing.
  • Check smoke and carbon monoxide alarms; the state requires a certificate for one-family and two-family sales, valid six months.
  • Repair visible safety problems, such as loose rails and missing detectors, before the appointment.

The construction office keeps blueprints of a house for 10 years, so ask it for plans if you did work and need to show permits to a buyer. The Land Use Office can tell you a property's zoning designation.

sections.h2: How do property taxes and appeals work in Hamilton Township?
sections.html:
The Mercer County Board of Taxation at 640 South Broad Street in Trenton certifies assessments and hears appeals. Regular appeals are due by April 1, and added or omitted assessment appeals are due December 1, with in-person filing accepted from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Assessment postcards go out at the end of January, so review yours before deciding to file.

Mercer County's Property Information Portal lets owners look up property record cards, sales, deeds and tax information, which helps you find comparable sales near your street before you decide whether to file.

Ask the township tax collector for a written payoff before closing.

sections.h2: What does it cost to sell in Hamilton Township, and where is the deed recorded?
sections.html:
The seller owes the state Realty Transfer Fee when the deed is recorded. For a price above $350,000 the schedule is $2.90 per $500 on the first $150,000, $4.25 per $500 up to $200,000 and $4.80 per $500 up to $550,000, so a $450,000 sale comes to about $3,695. The Mercer County Clerk's Office adds that deeds above $1,000,000 recorded since July 10, 2025 are subject to a revised fee under a new state law.

The Mercer County Clerk records real estate transfers at 209 South Broad Street in Trenton, and title searchers and the public can view a property's history in its records room or online. A New Jersey resident seller signs the GIT/REP-3, while nonresident sellers owe an estimated Gross Income Tax payment of at least 2 percent of the price.

  • Realty Transfer Fee, by the state schedule.
  • Mortgage and lien payoffs.
  • Your share of the quarter's property tax.
  • Certificate and inspection fees set by the township.

sections.h2: Which roads, trains and schools serve Hamilton Township buyers?
sections.html:
Hamilton is the only New Jersey municipality hosting Interstate 95 and both auxiliary routes, I-195 and I-295, plus U.S. Routes 130 and 206 and Routes 29, 33 and 156. The township is about 65 miles from New York City and 35 miles from Philadelphia. The Hamilton train station on Sloan Avenue, off I-295 Exit 65B, serves NJ Transit's Northeast Corridor and recorded 3,635 average weekday boardings in 2025, the eighth-highest in the state.

The Hamilton Township School District runs 23 schools with three high schools, Nottingham (North), Hamilton West and Steinert (East), and reported 11,816 students in the 2021 to 2022 school year. Water comes from Aqua New Jersey or Trenton Water Works, so confirm which utility serves the house.

faqs.q: What approval do I need to sell a house in Hamilton Township, Mercer County?
faqs.a: A Certificate of Approval from the Office of Housing Inspection and Landlord Compliance is required before a change of occupancy. Apply through the township's portal or with the office's paper forms.

faqs.q: Where do I appeal my assessment in Hamilton Township?
faqs.a: File with the Mercer County Board of Taxation at 640 South Broad Street in Trenton by April 1. Added or omitted assessment appeals are due December 1.

faqs.q: Does Hamilton Township inspect for lead before a sale?
faqs.a: No, the township does not test houses for lead on request. An owner who wants one has to hire a private inspector.

faqs.q: Where is a Hamilton Township deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Mercer County Clerk's Office, 209 South Broad Street in Trenton. Deeds over $1,000,000 recorded since July 10, 2025 carry a revised fee under the new state law.

faqs.q: Why does my Hamilton address say Trenton?
faqs.a: The Postal Service officially treats many Hamilton addresses as Trenton, even though the property is in Hamilton Township. Use the township name when you advertise so buyers find the right tax and school information.
